A QR code on a cannabis package should point at something checkable — not just a claim printed on the box. StrainChain hashes each batch record at registration and generates a QR code per lot, so scanning it surfaces the actual event ledger behind that batch: cultivated, harvested, lab-tested, packaged, transferred, received at the dispensary. Each stage is its own record, not a single end-of-chain attestation a buyer just has to trust.

Underneath that ledger sits a direct Michigan METRC integration — pulling transfer manifests from the state's seed-to-sale API, with retry and fallback built in, instead of a distributor's compliance record being a spreadsheet someone re-keys after the fact.

This is Michigan METRC today, not every state's system — the sync is real, not a demo screenshot, and we're not pretending it covers more ground than it does.

reddit.title: What's actually behind the QR code on a cannabis package's compliance label?
reddit.body:
I work on StrainChain, a cannabis-provenance tool. The part I want feedback on: a QR code on a package is only as good as what it points at, so batch registration hashes the record and generates a QR per lot that resolves to the batch's actual event ledger — cultivated, harvested, lab-tested, packaged, transferred, received at the dispensary — as separate, ordered records rather than one end-of-chain attestation.

That ledger sits on top of a Michigan METRC integration that pulls transfer manifests directly from the state's seed-to-sale API (with retry/fallback), rather than someone re-keying a manifest into a spreadsheet after the fact.

Right now this is Michigan METRC specifically — I haven't built out other states' systems yet, and I don't want to imply otherwise.

For people running compliance in other METRC states: if a QR code on a label resolved to a real per-stage ledger instead of a static certificate, would that change how you audit a batch, or is METRC's own manifest already enough for you?

https://strainchain.io/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=strainchain-chain-of-custody&utm_content=b

Disclosure: I work on this project.
